cards.title: What LumenNous Means By Gnosticism
cards.summary: The app uses Gnostic language as a field of exploration, not as one fixed creed. Ancient sources differ across Sethian, Valentinian, Thomasine, Hermetic and later streams.

cards.title: The Source, Monad And Pleroma
cards.summary: These names point toward ultimate origin and fullness in several ancient texts. LumenNous presents them as depth-layer language users can choose, not required belief.

cards.title: Sophia And Divine Wisdom
cards.summary: Sophia means wisdom. In some Gnostic texts she becomes a dramatic figure of descent, longing, error, lament and restoration. The app uses Sophia carefully as wisdom imagery.

cards.title: Why Lament Belongs In Prayer
cards.summary: The Psalms preserve complaint, grief and unanswered pain as real prayer. LumenNous should not rush sorrow into gratitude or resolution.

cards.title: Affirmations Without Forced Positivity
cards.summary: The best-supported affirmation model is values-based and compassionate, not inflated self-praise. Strong positive statements can backfire for people who do not believe them.

cards.title: Breath, Rhythm And Sacred Recitation
cards.summary: The strongest bridge between sacred sound and physiology is rhythm and pacing, especially slow recitation near six breaths per minute. Frequency healing claims need strong caution.

cards.title: Aramaic Prayer And Translation Honesty
cards.summary: Syriac and Aramaic prayer lineages are real and beautiful, but modern devotional renderings should not be presented as exact translations of Jesus' original words.

cards.title: Chakras And Subtle-Energy Content
cards.summary: Classical subtle-body traditions are complex. The familiar seven-colour chakra system is a modern synthesis, so the app must attribute it clearly and avoid medical or frequency claims.

cards.title: Prayer Is Not Medical Treatment
cards.summary: Prayer and meditation can support reflection and steadiness, but the app must not claim to diagnose, cure or replace professional care.

cards.title: Modern Gnosticism And Technology
cards.summary: Modern writers sometimes use Gnostic patterns to interpret technology, media and alienation. This is useful cultural interpretation, not evidence about ancient communities.
